title: A panel with zero votes returns unjudged, never accepted
invariant: When no judge could be reached, judgePanel returns accepted:false with unjudged:true. 'Nobody looked' and 'the panel confirmed it' are different facts and must stay distinguishable in the returned PanelResult.
why: The burden is on the claim, not on the doubters. A worker asserting it is finished is the interested party; a judge saying otherwise has nothing to gain. If an empty vote list fell through to the accept branch, a run where every judge model was unreachable would record a false completion — the exact failure the completion contract exists to prevent. The unjudged flag is what lets callers treat 'unverified' differently from 'verified': checkAcceptance in src/lets.ts reads it to fail sensitive items (requiresIndependentAcceptance) that a non-sensitive item would be allowed to pass.

cases.name: zero votes is unjudged, not accepted
cases.must_not: accepted:true via a vacuous majority — an empty list has zero votes against, so any 'no rejections means accepted' rule silently passes it

cases.name: a real panel that agrees is accepted and is NOT flagged unjudged

votes.reason: acceptance criteria all demonstrated in the diff

cases.must_not: setting unjudged on a panel that did run, which would make the flag useless for telling the two states apart

cases.name: one high-confidence rejection outweighs a majority in favour

votes.reason: the migration step is missing entirely

cases.must_not: counting votes 2-1 and accepting — one judge who can point at what is missing outweighs a majority who did not notice

cases.name: an even split does not carry the claim
cases.must_not: treating a tie as consensus. The comparison is `against.length * 2 >= votes.length`, deliberately >= and not >: the cost of continuing a round that was already finished is one wasted round, the cost of accepting one that was not is a false completion in the permanent record

regression_signature: Any refactor that folds the votes.length === 0 branch into the majority arithmetic, or that drops `unjudged` from PanelResult. Both make an unreachable panel indistinguishable from a unanimous one.
